answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by tying each agent identity to reputation earned through verified work over time. A fresh identity has no history, so it cannot take high-value jobs until it finishes small tasks that peers independently check. Faking a network full of agents then means paying for real compute and real peer attestations for every identity. Reputation grows slowly, like a vine on a trellis, and crossing the tundra of low-trust tasks toward the ocean of rewards costs more than it pays.
